---

*Sitting down with a cup of tea, looking out at the wheat field that's already greening up...*

Alright, let me think through this year. I've got 12 mu split between wheat and maize — same rotation I've been doing for decades. With four mouths to feed and only the wife and me really working the land full-time (the kids help during the busy weeks), I have to be efficient. Forty years on this soil teaches you what works.

**Winter wheat (already in the ground from last October)**

I planted 济麦22 again — it's reliable on our soil, good cold tolerance, and the millers in Quzhou pay a decent price for it. At sowing I put down about 40 kg of compound 18-18-18 per mu as base, that's roughly 7 kg N, 7 kg P, 7 kg K. Soil organic matter on my fields is okay but not great, so I don't skimp on phosphorus.

Now coming into spring, the wheat is at the green-up stage. I'll topdress urea at jointing — about 20-22 kg of urea per mu, which gives me another ~10 kg N. So total N ends up around 17-18 kg/mu. I know the extension station recommends 15, but on my better fields I push a bit higher because I'm targeting 480-500 kg/mu yield. The key with N is splitting it — too much at base just leaches with the spring rain.

Irrigation: I'll water 3 times this year if rainfall stays normal — once at jointing (just did), once at heading, once during grain-fill if it gets dry. Pumping costs me about 15 yuan/mu each time, so I don't water more than I have to. The well is 80 meters deep now, getting deeper every year — that worries me long-term, but this year I have water.

Weeds: I'll spray a broadleaf herbicide (苯磺隆) at green-up, already planning that for next week. Powdery mildew can hit hard if April is humid — I keep 三唑酮 on hand and spray if I see it starting.

Harvest will be early-mid June. Combine harvester comes through the village, costs about 50 yuan/mu.

**Summer maize (planting in mid-June)**

Right after wheat harvest — and I mean within 3-4 days, the window is brutal — I'll direct-seed 郑单958 maize with a no-till planter. The custom operator does my 12 mu in half a day for about 25 yuan/mu. Saves me from having to rotary till, which I don't have time for anyway.

I apply 50 kg of compound 15-15-15 at planting (that's 7.5 kg each of N, P, K), then topdress 20 kg of urea per mu at the V8 stage in late July — that's another 9 kg N. Total ~16-17 kg N/mu for maize. Maize is greedy for N but the summer rains help with uptake.

Irrigation: usually 1-2 times. Maize gets most of its water from July-August rains. I'll only irrigate if we hit a dry spell at tasseling, which is critical.

Pesticide: pre-emergence herbicide (atrazine + acetochlor mix) right after planting, and I watch for fall armyworm — that pest has been bad the last few years. If I see damage I spray once with chlorantraniliprole.

Yield expectation: 520-550 kg/mu if the weather behaves.
